newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-WOKING HOLD COVENTRY TO DRAW IN FA CUP UPSET.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WOKING HOLD COVENTRY TO DRAW IN FA CUP UPSET.

text.p: Minor league Woking equalised in the last minute to hold premier league Coventry City to a 1-1 draw on an astonishing day of surprises in the F.A. Cup on Saturday.

Steve Thompson scored for the visitors with just seconds remaining of their postponed third round tie after Coventry appeared to have done enough to save themselves any embarrassment with a 75th-minute opener from Eoin Jess.

Brave Hednesford Town, the only other minor league side involved in the competition, pressed multi-million pound premier league Middlesbrough all the way at the Riverside Stadium before losing their fourth round tie 3-2.
Middlesbrough needed two goals in the last two minutes from Jan-Aage Fjortoft and Fabrizio Ravanelli to win after Hednesford had taken an early lead.
There were upset wins for second division Wrexham whose 90th-minute goal from substitute Kevin Russell gave them a 1-0 victory at premier league West Ham in a third round replay at Upton Park.
Bradford City, just two off the bottom of the first division, also scored an upset win beating premier league Everton, the 1995 Cup winners, 3-2 in a fourth round match at Goodison Park.

Cup holders Manchester United, bidding to become the first club ever to appear in four successive Cup finals, appeared to have given themselves a fifth round place when Paul Scholes headed them ahead after 89 minutes against Wimbledon at Old Trafford.
But the London side defied the odds and equalised with only seconds to go when Robbie Earle headed past Peter Schmeichel for an unlikely equaliser.
